content: Is there / will there be API for natural transformations and modules over monads, not at the level of category theory, but at the level of functional programming?
Probably not. We also don’t have comonads afaik.
At least leansearch.net only returns declarations in the category theory library
Isn't the monadlift class basically a natural transformation?
:search: MonadLiftT, instMonadLiftT, and 174 more
Ah, it's missing the naturality square, but that is common practice when interpreting these things in programming, afaict

Yes, monad lifts are natural transformations, but I was more so thinking of just having them as morphisms of (functional programming) functors.

Also by modules over monads, I'm thinking of a "monad-like" universe-level function where the "bind" makes use of another monad in the second argument, e.g. if f is a functor and m is a monad, then f ∘ m would be a module over the monad m, where the "bind" is of type f (m α) → (α → m β) → f (m β) and is defined in the usual way.

I'd like to see more FP abstractions like comonads and modules over monads, maybe Cslib would be a good place for it? Specifically the Foundations/Control folder which currently only has free monad stuff

Robin Arnez said:

There's docs#LawfulMonadLift for the naturality

well more precisely docs#LawfulMonadLift says it preserves pure and bind but you can derive naturality from this. But natural transformations between functors would be a good definition to have explicitly
Alright - I'll try to implement them and get a PR going for this. I think I'll probably do it for Mathlib though.

I don’t have a preference but i suspect you’ll have a much easier time getting it reviewed in cslib. there has been some disagreement about whether things like this belong in mathlib at all and i’ve heard mention of getting rid of the Control folder entirely (which i don’t think will happen, but i think it means it’s less likely to see PRs get merged there)
